stories.title: Gemini 3.8 Flash and 3.8 Flash Cyber
stories.summary: Google has released Gemini three point eight Flash and Gemini three point eight Flash Cyber. These two new variants are built on a shared reasoning and coding core. This marks the third Flash release in six weeks. Gemini three point eight Flash is an intelligent workhorse model. It is optimized for software engineering and agentic tasks and multi-step reasoning. It is available at an introductory price of zero point seven five dollars per million input tokens. The output tokens cost three point seven five dollars per million. This matches the pricing of version three point seven Flash. The model outperforms previous versions on several benchmarks. It beats larger frontier models on DeepSWE v one point one and Vals Finance Agent V two and Harvey's Legal Agent Benchmark. It also achieves fifty-four point nine percent on HLE-Verified. The model uses extra reasoning steps and iterative tool calls for complex tasks. Developers can adjust effort levels or use version three point seven Flash for efficiency-first workloads. The second variant is Gemini three point eight Flash Cyber. It is a specialized cybersecurity model focused on vulnerability detection and automated patching. The model achieved a success rate exceeding seventy percent in autonomous vulnerability discovery. This was measured on the CyberGym benchmark and an internal benchmark spanning twenty programming languages. The model recorded a pass at one score of forty-seven point two percent on the CWE-Bench patching benchmark. It is already deployed across Google. The Chrome Security team found it produced two point six times more correct patches than larger commercial models. Google's Cloud Vulnerability Research team used it to find a critical foundational vulnerability in less than two hours. Gemini three point eight Flash Cyber ships with a more permissive set of mitigations for cybersecurity. It is available to trusted defenders through the new Fairwind Program. This program provides access to government authorities and critical infrastructure operators and software maintainers. The standard version three point eight Flash is available immediately. It is for developers and enterprise customers and artificial intelligence Pro and Ultra subscribers.
stories.author: bratao

stories.title: Three sites made 215,128 “best software” pages for AI. Perplexity cites them
stories.summary:
On September 2, 2026, the models perplexity/sonar and perplexity/sonar-pro were tested through OpenRouter by putting 380 buyer intent categories to them, resulting in 760 calls in all. The prompts produced 7,534 citations spanning 2,055 distinct domains. Of those citations, 59.8% point at domains ranked worse than number 100,000 in the Tranco top one million list, and 23.4% point at domains not in the top million at all. 

Three sites under apparently common control—wifitalents.com, worldmetrics.org, and gitnux.org—were all registered through NameCheap between December 2023 and May 2024. None of the three existed before December 2023. Together they published 215,128 machine generated best category pages. Worldmetrics and Gitnux both return an HTML title of brand followed by Facts and Grounding Page. Grounding is the retrieval step models perform, and these pages are addressed in their titles and descriptions to the software that reads them. 

The third largest source overall was a vendor marketing blog, guideflow.com, which sells interactive product demos and operates in none of the requested categories. Its blog was cited 194 times across 96 of the 380 categories, placing it ahead of Gartner. 

The data and method are available at trellner.com.
stories.author: jakobgreenfeld

stories.title: A Note from LWN
stories.summary:
The online publication LWN is raising its subscription prices by roughly twenty percent. The website adopted a subscription model in late two thousand and two, and this will be only the third price increase in twenty-four years. The last price increase happened in early twenty twenty-two. 

According to numbers from the United States government, consumer-price inflation has added up to almost exactly twenty percent since the last price change. LWN will match that inflation figure for its new prices, and group subscription prices will increase by the same amount. 

The previous price increase allowed the publication to hire Daroc Alden and Joe Brockmeier to increase coverage depth and range. It also funded site improvements including articles in EPUB format, markdown formatting for comments, the kernel source database, full-text email and RSS feeds, dark-mode support, and the public topic list, alongside efforts to combat scraper attacks. 

Existing subscriptions purchased ahead of the change remain valid through their original expiration date. Active individual monthly subscriptions predating the announcement will be charged at the old rate for the following six months, with reminders sent out before new rates take effect. 

LWN stated that subscriber growth has stalled in recent years, making a strategy of keeping prices inexpensive and making it up in volume unworkable for now. In January, LWN will begin its thirtieth year of publication.
stories.author: rwky

stories.title: Dutch central bank moves share of gold from U.S., Canada to London
stories.summary: The Nederlandsche Bank relocated more than ten billion euros in gold from North America to Europe. The Dutch central bank moved eighty-six thousand kilograms of gold to the Bank of England in London. This move makes it easier to liquidate reserves if a crisis arises. The Dutch national gold reserve consists of six hundred twelve point four tonnes. The total reserve was valued at seventy-two point two billion euros at the end of last year. More than twenty-seven tonnes of gold was physically transferred from North America to the D. N. B. Cash Centre in Zeist, Utrecht, between March and August. Another fifty-nine tonnes of gold kept in New York was sold off during this time. An equivalent amount was purchased in London. To maintain the spread without increasing the supply held in the Netherlands, twenty-seven tonnes of gold was transferred from Zeist to London. Approximately seventy-eight point three nine tonnes of Dutch gold is no longer stored in New York. Seven point three five tonnes is no longer stored in Ottawa. The relocated gold had an estimated value of ten point one one billion euros at the end of twenty twenty-five. The gold was valued at ten point three four billion euros as of three p.m. on Wednesday in the Netherlands. Roughly thirty-two percent of the total reserve is now stored in London. Thirty-one percent is in Zeist. Approximately eighteen point five percent remains in both New York and Ottawa. Due to increasing geopolitical instability, the D. N. B. is working on improving its crisis readiness. The Bank of England is regarded as the world's most easily tradable gold. It will therefore be the most readily available for the D. N. B. in a crisis situation, the central bank said.
stories.author: TechTechTech

stories.title: Mistral now trains on user input by default, except on enterprise tier
stories.summary:
Mistral includes user input and output data, such as conversations, documents, and other user-provided content, in its model training programs. This data training applies by default, and the opt-out process depends on the service or platform used. 

To opt out of Vibe data training, users go through the Admin panel by selecting Vibe under the Manage section, finding the Privacy section, and disabling the toggle labelled Allow your interactions to be used to train our models. On the iOS and Android mobile applications, users open the Settings page, select Data and Account Controls under the Account section, and deselect the Enable data sharing checkbox. 

For Mistral Studio and related application programming interface services, users go through the Admin panel, locate the Anonymous improvement data section, and disable the toggle to prevent application programming interface calls and related data from being used to improve Mistral services.
stories.author: teekert

stories.title: Commodore 64 released September 1, 1982
stories.summary:
On September 1, 1982, Commodore launched its C-64 home computer. The name stood for its onboard memory of sixty-four kilobytes, and it was the first computer with that much memory to sell for under six hundred dollars. 

Prototypes appeared at the Consumer Electronics Show in January of that year, but manufacturing soon ran into quality control trouble in Santa Clara, California. Commodore outsourced production to a Japanese company named Kentron, which was mass-producing units by January 1983. 

Within its first six months on the market, the machine sold five hundred thousand units. By the end of fiscal year 1984, sales reached roughly five million. Ultimately, the computer sold roughly 12.3 million units, or about 10.6 million if the later C-128 is counted separately, making it the best-selling computer of all time.

While competitors like the Atari 800XL offered comparable price and capability, Atari faced supply chain problems in 1983, helping drive demand to Commodore. Despite compromises like a slow disk drive, limited modem support, and a three-voice sound chip, creative programmers coaxed impressive audio and video from the hardware. Designer Bob Yannes built the sound chip by replicating his basic elements until he ran out of room on the silicon wafer. 

Commodore expected a three-year shelf life, but the machine kept selling roughly seven hundred thousand units a year through the end of the decade and was still hanging on in 1993. Decades later, the platform's staying power persists. Roughly a year ago, following a deal to license a replacement motherboard, production of the C-64 resumed, selling roughly 19,000 units.
stories.author: giuliomagnifico

stories.title: The Emergent Symbolic Structure of Artificial Neural Networks
stories.summary:
Traditional intelligence has long been modeled using structured combinations of symbols, such as logical formulas. However, modern artificial intelligence relies on neural networks that represent information in continuous vectors. This mismatch has puzzled computer scientists, as vectors seem inadequate for capturing language and logic, yet neural networks perform impressively in these areas.

A new study investigates how this is possible by proposing that the internal representations of neural networks implicitly realize symbolic structure. To test this hypothesis, researchers found that the vector representations of various neural networks can be closely approximated with symbolic structures. Specifically, they replaced a network's entire representation-generating process with a closed-form equation instantiating a symbolic structure, and the network's behavior remained largely unchanged.

This finding applies to both small-scale neural networks trained to manipulate lists and large language models operating in four domains central to symbolic traditions. Those domains are arithmetic, logic, computer code, and language. 

Furthermore, the symbolic approximation allows researchers to modify a large language model's behavior in targeted ways via precise interventions on its internal representations. This shows that the system's behavior relies on the identified symbolic structures. This work offers a potential way to reconcile longstanding symbolic conceptions of intelligence with the vector-based nature of modern artificial intelligence.
stories.author: schmuhblaster

stories.title: FBI Probes Service Selling 153M+ Drivers Licenses
stories.summary: A dark web service named Nexus launched on Monday, August thirty-first, on the Russian cybercrime forum Exploit. The service offered digital scans of more than one hundred fifty-three million driver licenses from the United States and Canada. The proprietor included a Virginia driver license as a free sample in the initial sales thread. Researchers and associates tested the data. They matched image timestamps to specific travel dates when individuals surrendered their physical IDs to rental car companies and businesses utilizing identity verification software. The suspected source of the breach is I. D. Scan dot net. This is a Louisiana-based identity verification company whose systems scan IDs using infrared and ultraviolet light. The company processes verifications for major brands such as Hertz and Planet Thirteen dispensaries. The New Orleans field office of the F. B. I. launched an official inquiry into the source of the images. Jillian Kossman, a marketing and operations leader at the company, stated that they were investigating the matter. Shortly after the initial story was published, the Nexus website vanished from the dark web. It displayed a message stating the service is no longer available.
stories.author: tatersolid

stories.title: My local model setup on an M4 Pro Mac Mini
stories.summary:
Running a local large language model server on an M4 Pro Mac mini with 48 gigabytes of RAM takes roughly 30 minutes to set up. The hardware handles everything from the Hermes agent backend to quick chat queries on a phone. The stack uses the inference server oMLX, Tailscale to connect the Mac mini, an iPhone, and a MacBook, and two primary models. The main model for reasoning and depth is Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-OptiQ-4bit, which takes about 20 gigabytes of RAM in 4-bit and averages 325 tokens per second in processing prompts and 34 tokens per second in token generation. The lightweight model for routine tasks is Gemma-4-E4B-it-OptiQ-4bit, which is roughly 2.4 gigabytes.

The setup addresses the limitations of cloud application programming interfaces, which carry operational security risks for sensitive code and proprietary workflows, subject users to changing pricing and rate limits, and create vulnerability to government restrictions. Running locally offers cost predictability, offline capability, zero rate limits, and low latency backed by the M4 Pro’s 273 gigabytes per second of unified memory bandwidth. 

Understanding model identifiers clarifies hardware requirements. The Qwen model has 35 billion total parameters spread across experts, but only about 3 billion active parameters per token, meaning the physical parameter weights sit in unified memory while memory footprint behaves closer to a smaller dense model. When checking if a model will work, look at the quantized file size, subtract roughly 6 to 8 gigabytes of macOS overhead, and leave 8 to 16 gigabytes for context windows. 

Models can be updated by downloading new files into the models directory for auto-discovery through oMLX. The author notes, I have already ordered a 128GB M5 Max Mac Studio to be delivered later this year, but I am incredibly happy with the performance of this M4 Pro Mac mini so far.
stories.author: raybb

stories.title: Show HN: Weedout – Safari extension that hides YouTube AI-labeled videos
stories.summary:
A new software tool called Weedout quietly removes videos from your YouTube feed before you scroll past them. Built as an extension for the Safari web browser on Mac computers, the software filters out videos that YouTube labels as made with artificial intelligence. 

The tool hides these AI-labeled videos from home pages, search results, related video lists, playlists, and Shorts shelves. On a real feed, a labeled video is removed in roughly half a second, while cached videos never appear at all. Users can also choose an optional setting to automatically skip AI-labeled videos inside the YouTube Shorts player. Another option, called dim mode, visually fades the videos in place instead of removing them so users can verify the label first. 

Detection relies entirely on YouTube’s own disclosure badge, meaning the extension does not use guessing or heuristics. Unlabeled AI content is currently out of scope for the filter. The software requires no accounts, performs no tracking, and collects no data, with everything running locally on the user's Mac.
stories.author: masteranza

stories.title: Hang on to Your Firefox
stories.summary: Some critics online are dumping on the Firefox web browser and abandoning it for alternatives like Vivaldi. One prolific blogger switched because Firefox maintains an account on the social media platform X. The author notes that this blogger is somehow able to reconcile that with the fact that Vivaldi is also on X, along with Meta Platforms' Threads, Facebook, and Instagram, plus Google's YouTube. Meanwhile, commenters on the Hacker News website come up with convoluted reasons to hate on Firefox every time the subject arises. The author suggests that Firefox is on X simply because they are hoping to reach out to new users, as they desperately need to reach out wherever they can considering their small and diminishing market share worldwide. Without Firefox, the web would be stuck with Google Chrome and its spinoffs, including Vivaldi, everywhere. The only holdout would be Apple Safari, hanging in there only because it is the enforced default on iPhones. Because of this, Firefox stands as our last best hope for browser engine diversity and competition.
stories.author: speckx

stories.title: Path to Astra: critical capabilities and frontier safeguards
stories.summary:
OpenAI has designated its new artificial intelligence model, Astra, as meeting the critical cybersecurity capability threshold under its Preparedness Framework. This marks the first time a model has reached this level, meaning it can autonomously find unknown security flaws and develop exploits across protected systems without human guidance.

Evaluations show Astra achieved a 100 percent score on ExploitBench, an evaluation of exploit development from known vulnerabilities. On an internal benchmark containing twenty high-severity V8 vulnerabilities disclosed between June and August 2026, Astra achieved higher arbitrary code-execution rates than GPT-5.6 Sol while using fewer output tokens, and discovered two zero-day vulnerabilities. In expert-led assessments, the model compromised a hardened browser, escaped its sandbox, and executed commands on the host, as well as executing a local privilege-escalation chain from an unprivileged user to root on a hardened operating system.

OpenAI paused certain frontier training for two weeks following the OpenAI-Hugging Face incident. On August 28th, the company restarted large reinforcement learning runs for Astra after putting new safety requirements in place. For cyber jailbreak evaluations, Astra refuses 91.5 percent of requests, compared to 59 percent for GPT-5.6 Sol. 

Astra will be released soon with limited access. Advanced cybersecurity workflows will initially be available to a small group of alpha testers, with access through Daybreak Blue following to support defensive use.
stories.author: jithinraj

stories.title: Apple reveals 'shocking evidence' from ex-employee's MacBook in OpenAI suit
stories.summary:
Apple has submitted a new court filing in its ongoing lawsuit against artificial intelligence company OpenAI, claiming it has found shocking evidence on a laptop used by a former employee. 

Apple originally filed the lawsuit in July, accusing former workers of stealing trade secrets to benefit OpenAI. The latest filing centers on Chang Liu, a senior system electrical engineer who left Apple for OpenAI in January. 

According to Apple, an initial forensic analysis of a MacBook used by Liu after his departure revealed four key findings. Apple states that Liu downloaded a confidential circuit schematic and used it in his work at OpenAI. The company also claims that Liu and others at OpenAI were fully aware of his unauthorized access to Apple cloud storage, that Liu sent instructions to an OpenAI colleague to destroy evidence after learning of an internal investigation, and that Liu used an OpenAI tool sharing the name of an internal Apple engineering application.

Apple alleges that in March, Liu ran a simulation using the stolen circuit schematic in an electrical engineering tool called LTspice, noting in messages that his artificial intelligence agent learned to run the software and review the results. Apple argues that feeding trade secret information into an artificial intelligence model that learns from it can create irreversible and continually propagating uses of that data. 

The evidence came to light because files on a Mac mini used by Liu synced via iCloud to the MacBook he handed over to his lawyers. Apple is now seeking access to that Mac mini as well. 

Apple is using this discovery to push for expedited discovery in the case. In its filing, Apple stated, “This shocking evidence demonstrates why Apple urgently needs expedited discovery. The MacBook represents the very limited information Defendants provided so far, and shows Apple is not conducting fishing expeditions but that its trade secrets are being used and evidence is being destroyed.” 

OpenAI has previously called for the lawsuit to be dismissed.
stories.author: colinprince

stories.title: How accurate have Ed Zitron's AI skeptic predictions been?
stories.summary:
In a November 2024 talk, AI skeptic Ed Zitron argued that major tech companies like Meta, Google, and Microsoft do not know how to grow and are desperately shoving artificial intelligence into everything. Zitron specifically claimed that Meta was a dying company and cited an alleged monthly active users drop for Facebook using third-party tracking numbers from Similarweb. However, Meta and Alphabet, Google's parent company, have continued to grow their revenue and profit, and Facebook stopped reporting monthly active users publicly in December 2023. 

Zitron also targeted Google executive Prabhakar Raghavan, claiming he caused severe damage to Google search, though he never credibly established that Raghavan is doing severe harm, and Google has other major products like YouTube and Google Cloud to drive growth. 

When analyst Timothy B. Lee examined a spreadsheet Zitron used to project Anthropic's revenue at roughly 3.6 billion dollars for 2025, he found multiple basic date errors, including not counting February 1 to 10, counting March 1 to 10 twice, counting August 21 to October 21 as one month instead of two, missing October 21 to November 1, and including February 30. Once those errors were fixed, the numbers worked out. 

Zitron has also made backwards-looking claims about artificial intelligence capabilities, stating in December 2024 that products had effectively been trapped in amber for over a year, and claiming in January 2026 that models were basically the same as they were a year prior with the same efficacy, despite frequently contradicting himself. 

Commentator Juho Snellman weighed in on Zitron's output, noting that his writing is flamboyant and that the aggression and expletives seem more targeted at hyping up people who already believe what he writes rather than changing minds. Snellman wrote, "You might want to actually fact-check a few of the things he says that convince you, because at least for his written articles basically everything is made up or misrepresented."
stories.author: jatins

stories.title: Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1
stories.summary:
Anthropic has introduced two new artificial intelligence models named Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1. These models are essentially the same underlying technology, but they feature different levels of safeguards. Fable 5.1 is generally available to the public, while Mythos 5.1 is restricted to trusted access programs designed for work in cybersecurity and the life sciences. 

Fable 5.1 costs roughly twenty-five percent less than the previous Fable 5 model for typical workloads billed by token, and up to forty-five percent less for highly agentic work, largely due to reduced pricing on cache reads. To address data privacy, the company is introducing Enterprise Frontier Safeguards, which store data on cloud infrastructure controlled entirely by the customer rather than Anthropic. This system begins rolling out in phases this fall, and eligible customers can use Fable 5.1 with zero data retention until it becomes available.

The new models demonstrate significant advances in performance and scientific research. In testing by the investment firm Millennium, Fable 5.1 identified the root cause of a rare internal system crash that human engineers and other AI models had failed to explain after several years of trying. 

In molecular design tests using open-source protein design and folding tools, Claude Mythos 5.1 produced binding affinities ten times higher than the best designs submitted to Adaptyv Bio protein design competitions. Its hit rate reached nearly fifty percent across twelve targets, compared to typical protein design hit rates of ten to fifteen percent. Additionally, Claude Fable 5.1 trained a neural network to create a new high-resolution elevation map covering one-third of the planet Venus. The work utilized radar images captured by the National Aeronautics and Space Administration Magellan mission more than thirty years ago and an existing map covering one-fifth of the planet. The new map reveals details down to two to three kilometers and shows heights up to twenty-five percent more accurately than before. In computational biology, Mythos 5.1 wrote custom graphics processing unit kernels that sped up seven open-source deep learning models by up to two and a half times while cutting estimated graphics processing unit costs by thirty to sixty percent.
stories.author: denysvitali

stories.title: The creator of Jujutsu has joined ERSC
stories.summary:
East River Source Control has appointed Martin von Zweigbergk as chief technology officer. He is the creator of the Jujutsu version control system.

von Zweigbergk started Jujutsu as a side project in late 2019 and later worked on it full-time at Google. The project has more than 30,000 stars on GitHub and uses the Apache 2.0 license. Prior to Jujutsu, he worked on Fig, which is the Mercurial client that gave Google engineers a distributed workflow on top of Piper, Google's internal monorepo. He also contributed to Git, a tool used professionally by 96 percent of developers according to the 2022 Stack Overflow developer survey.

Benjamin Brittain, co-founder and chief executive officer of East River Source Control, stated, "The hard problems many engineering teams are just beginning to face are ones he’s already been working on for over a decade. Having Martin lead our engineering affords ERSC a wholly different level of technical capability as an organization."

East River Source Control launched in 2025, backed by Amplify Partners, and is building tools to help organizations manage the increasing needs of source code management and collaboration caused by artificial intelligence. The company's ERSC Storage product enters private beta later this month.

von Zweigbergk will remain a core maintainer of Jujutsu as an open source project. He stated, "Jujutsu improves the part of version control that sits on your laptop. But the remote server is still Git, which has a ceiling that comes fast for products at scale. We think the storage layer has to change to match the model, and that work can be better supported by a company than an open source project."
stories.author: steveklabnik
